html:
SMTO-SCH-0002 — The schedules changed before SMTO could act on them

GUID: 692bc88c-d8d2-4c65-b36e-455b87c2f0eb
Slug: schedule-selection-changed
Domain: SCH · Subsystem: sch

What happened

  • Either the list of schedules you picked to delete changed after you reviewed it, or a Run now couldn't start the schedule's task. In both cases nothing was deleted and no task was started.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you were deleting schedules, select Review again in the deletion dialog and check the updated list before selecting Delete schedules. A schedule was added, changed or finished after you reviewed the list, so SMTO won't delete a set you haven't seen.
  2. If you selected Run now, select Recent runs on that schedule on the Schedules page and read the error shown for the failed run. The run record says what was missing when SMTO tried to start the task.
  3. Fix what the run record names, for example make sure the Gateway the schedule uses is switched on and connected. The schedule's saved settings must still point to something SMTO can use before it can start.
  4. Select Run now again once that is fixed. No task was started the first time, so running it again won't repeat any work.

What success looks like

  • The deletion completes and the schedules disappear, or Run now shows "Started a run" for the schedule.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't select all matching schedules and delete them blindly; review the list each time.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Either bulk schedule deletion found that the recomputed selection digest no longer matches the reviewed one (ScheduleSelectionChanged), or Run now failed before a task was created because the schedule's saved launch scope could not be resolved.

What this means

  • Bulk deletion recomputes a schedule-selection digest and finds a mismatch, or an event-trigger wrapper reports that saved execution scope could not be resolved for launch. Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.

Why this can happen

  • Bulk deletion recomputes a schedule-selection digest and finds a mismatch, or an event-trigger wrapper reports that saved execution scope could not be resolved for launch.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish changed selection from launch-scope failure using the owning route and outcome.

How to fix it

  • For bulk delete, re-run the preview to obtain a new selection digest and confirm the reviewed set. For Run now (launch_failed: run status failed with no task_id), inspect the schedule's recent run record for the launch error, resolve the captured scope cause such as a missing Gateway, model route or workspace, then trigger again.
  • Refresh the exact selection or inspect the saved launch-scope failure before using the supported action again.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A current exact selection is confirmed, or the actual saved launch-scope problem is resolved.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Schedule configuration and temporal checks do not themselves launch deferred work. Existing event/request identities, captured authority and original execution receipts remain authoritative; diagnostic rendering does not poll time or mutate scheduling state.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
